title: Round-Trip Sync with GitHub
description: Push your local commits to GitHub, simulate a teammate's change by editing on GitHub web, and pull that change back down to your computer.
steps: In `hcc-git-practice`, push your local commits: `git push -u origin main`
Open your repository page on GitHub in your browser — confirm your files, commits, and README are live!
On GitHub, click on `README.md` and click the pencil icon to edit it
Add a new line: `* Contributed via GitHub web editor`
Now return to your local terminal inside `hcc-git-practice`
Run `git fetch origin` — notice Git downloaded remote info without modifying your local file yet
Run `git pull origin main` — observe your local `README.md` update automatically with the new line!
Check `git log --oneline` to see the remote commit in your local history
expected_output: Terminal confirms 'Fast-forward' merge and local `README.md` now contains the edit made on GitHub.
tips: The `-u` in `git push -u origin main` sets the upstream tracking reference so future pushes only require `git push`.
Always run `git pull` at the start of your workday before starting new code to ensure you have teammates' latest work.
